PROJECT COSTS

The DPWH projects approved by the NEDA Board include the
P8.55-billion ($190.29-million)* Cagayan De Oro River flood risk management project
The P8.55 Billion DPWH Flood Risk Management Project for Cagayan De Oro River comes in three (3) contract packages and involves the construction of 11,928 meters earth dike, 3,259 meters concrete flood wall including 1,449 meters reinforced concrete/masonry slope protection, 2,756 meters of new road and raising of existing road for evacuation, installation of three (3) steel slide gates and 19 flap gates, improvement of Kagayan River, and construction of retarding basin, concrete box/pipe culverts and headwall and drainage outlets.
PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
Involves implementation of the following structural (which is primarily river improvement in nature) and nonstructural measures:
1. Structural Measures
1.1 Construction of new dike/retaining wall
1.2 Installation of gate and drainage outlets
1.3 Construction of new road/raising of existing road for evacuation
1.4 Improvement of Kagayan Bridge
1.5 Construction of retarding basin
1.6 Periodic monitoring of river cross section and regular maintenance dredging/channel excavation
2. Non-Structural Measures
2.1 Preparation/Update of flood hazard map, evacuation planning
2.2 Flood Forecasting and Warning System (FFWS)
2.3 Community Based Flood Early Warning System (CBFEWS)
2.4 Information campaign and publicity for the project (Structural Measures)
2.5 Technical assistance for land use regulation for habitual inundation area
2.6 Technical assistance for riparian forest establishment in the agricultural lands
2.7 Technical assistance for mangrove forest establishment along the coastal areas

The objective of the Project is to mitigate flood risk in Cagayan de Oro River Basin through the construction of flood protection measures, and thereby contributing to the sustainable and stable economic development in Cagayan de Oro River Basin.

Bulletin No. 3 on Typhoon “URSULA”
Issued at 3:00 PM, December 25, 2019
 
"URSULA" MAINTAINS ITS STRENGTH AS IT MOVES TOWARDS SOUTHERN PORTION OF MINDORO PROVINCES.
 
Typhoon "URSULA" is bringing destructive wind and strong rainfall over Caluya Islands. Moreover, its eyewall will affect the southern portion of Mindoro in the succeeding hours.

Occasional to frequent heavy with intermittent intense rainfall will be experienced over Aklan, Antique, Capiz, Romblon, Calamian Islands, Cuyo Islands, and Mindoro Provinces until tonight. Meanwhile, light to moderate rainfall with isolated heavy rainshowers during thunderstorms is forecasted over Bicol Region, rest of Western Visayas, CALABARZON, Marinduque, Aurora and the northern portion of mainland Palawan. 

On the other hand, moderate to strong wind has been affecting the Metro Manila and Bataan this afternoon. In addition, destructive typhoon-force winds to begin affecting Mindoro Provinces this afternoon; Calamian islands between this afternoon and evening.

Damages and losses in the agriculture sector are expected from Bicol Region and Visayas regions due to the Typhoon.

Moreover, damage assessment was put on hold due to flood and will be conducted as soon as the weather conditions permit.
